title: Lepapata (kudu horn)
summary: The lepapata is a horn made from a greater kudu or sable antelope, used for celebrations and warning calls. The twisted horn is blown through a mouth hole to sound a loud signal, and the player can reach a few notes of the overtone series by tightening the lips.
howToPlay: Four notes of the horn are lit along it, the higher ones nearer the mouth hole.
A band of breath runs from the mouth to the note you strike, and rings of sound leave the opening.
Long notes swell slowly: strike close to the beat and let them ring.
rules: A call is a line of long notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It carries far over open country, which is why it is used for signals as well as for music.
credits: Tradition: the lepapata; calls written for this game
